Amount.description: A sum of money or a price per unit of a cost method, never negative, such as a budget, a minimum spend, or a CPM. It is in the currency of the `currency` member of the object that carries it, and the cost method says what a rate is per.

BareTerm.description: A term or word written bare, letters and digits joined by underscores, such as `modeled`, `daily`, or `30d`, as the specification's examples write it where the text lists no values and states no form.

CalendarDate.description: A calendar date, written as an RFC 3339 `full-date`, `YYYY-MM-DD`, such as `2026-10-06`, as the specification's examples write a flight's start and end. A date names no instant until a time zone reads it, and the text names none for a flight.

CatalogRef.description: A version-pinned reference to an entry in a seller-maintained catalog, written `<seller_namespace>/<collection>/<entry_id>@<version>`, such as `examplepub/audiences/smb-decision-makers@3`. No part is empty or holds a `/`, an `@`, a space, or a control character.

CatalogReference.description: A reference that stands in for an inline value, given as the `catalog_ref` of the catalog entry that holds the value.

Count.description: A whole number of things, never negative and at most 2^53 − 1, such as impressions, options, or a proposal's revisions, which its `version` counts.

CurrencyCode.description: An ISO 4217 alphabetic currency code, such as `USD`.

DayName.description: A day of the week, named in lowercase English, from `monday` to `sunday`.

DaypartWindow.description: A window of the week in which a line item's ads may serve, read on the line item's clock, as Google Ad Manager writes a day part. On each day `days[]` names, the window runs from `start` up to `end`, which is exclusive and later than `start`. `start` is never `24:00`, the end of the day.

Domain.description: A domain name, written as lowercase A-labels with at least two labels, a top-level label that starts with a letter, and no trailing dot, such as `examplepub.example`.

Duration.description: A length of time, written as an ISO 8601 duration in the grammar of RFC 3339 Appendix A, such as `PT48H`.

ExternalId.description: The identity of a record, a code, or a version that another system or list defines, such as a registry entry, a DSP seat, a geo code, a content category, a published document's version, or a field of the specification, named by its path as the specification's tables write it, carried as that system writes it. A receiver compares it by exact string equality and doesn't parse it; the field's description names where it comes from.

FormatId.description: The ID of a creative format in the format registry, namespaced by channel and written `<channel>/<format>`, such as `display/300x250` or `audio/host-read-30s`. Neither part is empty or holds a `/`, a space, or a control character. A receiver compares it by exact string equality.

Fraction.description: A proportion from 0 to 1, such as 0.7 for 70 %.

Identifier.description: The identity of a record a party mints, such as a proposal or a line item, written as any string, as the specification types it. The text states no form, so a receiver compares two identities by exact string equality.

NamespacedTerm.description: A term outside a vocabulary's core list, written `<domain>:<term>`, where the domain is the definer's identity domain, such as `examplepub.example:podcast_host_read`.

PercentChange.description: A relative change to a price in percent, from −100 up, such as 10 for a 10 % surcharge or −5 for a 5 % discount.

PriceAdjustment.description: A signed change to a price or a sum of money, such as the change an option makes to the CPM, or a flat surcharge or discount. A negative value lowers the price.

PriceDelta.description: The change in price when the buyer selects an option outside `included[]`, given as exactly one of a change to the CPM, a flat change, or a change in percent.

Text.description: Prose for people and agents to read. A receiver doesn't parse it or compare it.

TimeOfDay.description: A civil time of day, written `HH:MM` from `00:00` to `24:00`, read on the line item's clock. `24:00` is the end of the day, so it ends a window and never starts one.

Timestamp.description: A point in time, written as an RFC 3339 date-time with a UTC offset, such as `2026-10-25T09:00:00Z`. It follows RFC 3339's grammar, with a `T` or `t` between the date and the time and an offset of `Z`, `z`, `+hh:mm`, or `-hh:mm`, never a space, `+05`, or `+0500`. Several spellings name one instant, such as `Z` and `+00:00`, so a receiver compares two Timestamps as instants, not as strings.

Url.description: An absolute `https` URL that a receiver may fetch.
